title: Time-bounded undecidability of unary halting
statement: For every effective machine code $c$, every finite-state Turing machine $M$ over the binary alphabet, and every function $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, $M$ does not decide the unary language whose words have all bits equal to $1$ and whose length $n$ satisfies: the binary expansion of $n$ is $1$ followed by a suffix $s$, and the halting predicate for $c$ accepts $s$, within time bound $T$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$T$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers
replaced:
For every effective machine code $c$, every finite-state Turing machine $M$ over the
binary alphabet, and every function $T$ from the natural numbers to the natural numbers,
$M$ does not decide within time bound $T$ the unary language whose accepted lengths are
those $n$ for which the binary expansion of $n$ begins with $1$ followed by a suffix $s$
such that the halting predicate for $c$ accepts $s$.
